481	a claim against Moshe Rabbeinu.
482	Why?
483	They said, this rabbi has no pedigree.
484	HaShem said to them, what do you mean he has no pedigree?
485	This is Moshe Rabbeinu, son of Amram: "A man of the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi." How can you say he has no pedigree?
486	They said, excuse us, who is his mother?
487	He said to them, what, who is his mother?
488	Yocheved, she was a righteous woman, what do you mean who is his mother?
489	They said, true, but Amram divorced his wife Yocheved.
490	And Yocheved went and married Elitzafan, and bore from him
491	Eldad and Medad.
492	Therefore Eldad and Medad are brothers of Moshe from the same mother but not the same father.
493	These are Eldad and Medad, and so the Ramban writes as well.
494	Afterwards Elitzafan and Yocheved decided they were not a match.
495	She was divorced from him.
496	And she returned to Amram.
497	So Moshe Rabbeinu is a son, when she returned to Amram, she bore Moshe
498	Rabbeinu.
499	So Moshe Rabbeinu is the son of one who retook his divorced wife after her remarriage, which is forbidden.
500	Did you understand the move that happened here?
501	In the Torah it is forbidden to do such a thing.
502	Why is it forbidden?
503	If a man divorced his wife, and she went and married someone else, and now she was divorced
504	from him, and she wants to return to the first one, her first husband, she cannot do that according to the Torah.
505	Why?
506	So that people won't swap wives.
507	How does that work?
508	Say, here I am, say there are two couples, me and my wife and another
509	man and his wife.
510	Now, God forbid, I set my eye on his wife, and he, God forbid, set his eye on my wife.
511	What do we do so that everything is clean, kosher, Torah-law at its strictest?
512	I divorce her, he divorces her.
513	I marry his wife, he marries my wife.
514	We do what we want, then I divorce her, he divorces her.
515	I take back my wife and he takes back his wife.
516	And everything is perfectly by the book, there is no prohibition here.
517	See, that is why the Torah was already wise, and said there is no such thing.
518	One who retakes his divorced wife after her remarriage, if she has already remarried, he can no longer take her back, so that there will be no
519	swapping of wives.
520	Did you understand this trick?
